title: VDCores Qwen3 1.7B Runtime LD Warp Address Diagnostic
command: Build tmp/baselines/vdcores with DAE_DEBUG_PRINT=64 and a temporary ldwarp address print, then run QWEN1P7B_NO_PREFETCH=all compute-sanitizer memcheck python app/python/qwen3_1p7b/sched.py --hf-cache-dir <shared-hf-cache> --debug-num-layers 1 --debug-stop-after final_rms -N 1 --launch on H200.
observation: SM64 emitted a runtime load-warp direct 1D load for slot 0, bar 0, addr 0x761ba2034000, size 4096. The first compute-sanitizer invalid 4096-byte cp_async_bulk read reports the same address in block (68,0,0), so the failing address is the direct 1D address consumed by the runtime load warp after instruction upload.
blocker: The runtime load warp consumes the same direct 1D address that compute-sanitizer reports as the first invalid 4096-byte cp_async_bulk read, so VDCores still cannot provide correctness or queue/resource-policy timing. The remaining blocker is why this runtime-consumed global address is outside sanitizer allocation tracking or otherwise unmapped during launch.

summary.tool: compute-sanitizer memcheck plus temporary DAE_DEBUG_PRINT=64 ldwarp address print
rules_out: load warp consuming a different direct 1D address than the first memcheck invalid read
static Python-side MInst address provenance as sole cause
summary.next_debug_target: explain why the direct 1D global address consumed by the runtime load warp is outside sanitizer allocation tracking or otherwise unmapped during VDCores launch
